messages:
liam (cust-success): FYI escalation from Acme Corp. they reported a big billing spike yesterday and say some SSO users still had access after being deprovisioned via SCIM. request ids attached, missing audit lines for the window. can we triage?

maria (support): Thanks. Can you paste the sample request IDs and the exact error body they saw? Also need the tenant id + approximate time window.

liam (cust-success): Tenant: tenant_acme_72. Window: 2024-10-11 02:12-02:45 UTC. Sample req id: r_0a9f3b2c. Customer forwarded this response body from their app: 

```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "ERR_KMS_UNWRAP",
  "message": "HSM UNWRAP FAILED: slot 3 timed out",
  "request_id": "r_0a9f3b2c"
}
```

They also attached an embed request that latched and retried ~30s later, which seems to have caused duplicate token billing.

maria (support): Noted. @tom can you check the runtime logs for that tenant/time for KMS unwrap failures and any request retries? Also can we confirm whether audit export for that window includes those requests? customer wants retention proof for legal. :eyes:

tom (eng-sre): Looking. Quick check in ingest logs shows a cluster-wide HSM timeout spike around 02:14 UTC correlating with heavy embedding throughput from tenant_acme_72. I see repeated 5xx returned at the load-balancer level which caused client retries. Pulling the unwrap traces now.

noah (eng-runtime): From runtime side: we had a short KMS proxy failover at 02:13:58 -> 02:15:10 UTC. Some workers reported unwrap latency > 10s which caused the request handler to return 502. I'm attaching a small log snippet.

```
[02:14:01] worker-07 tenant_acme_72 req=r_0a9f3b2c unwrap_ms=10234 result=ERR_KMS_UNWRAP
[02:14:02] worker-07 tenant_acme_72 req=r_0a9f3b2d retry_count=1 status=502
[02:14:35] worker-02 tenant_acme_72 req=r_0a9f3b2e embed_tokens=4096 duration_ms=1250
```

anya (security): For the audit/retention ask: we need to confirm if the audit export contains the unwrap error and token accounting for that window. If audit lines are missing, we must prepare a signed statement for legal and preserve HSM/KMS traces. @maria — do we have an export/retention policy override for this customer?

maria (support): No override on file. Standard retention is 90 days. Customer says they started a data retention request yesterday and needs evidence sooner. I'll open a priority export.

liam (cust-success): Also they claim several users that were deprovisioned via SCIM still showed as active in the console for ~12 minutes. Could that be a lag in provisioning or a separate auth cache issue?

tom (eng-sre): Good catch. I see SCIM deprov events at 02:08:21 for users U1234/U1235 but the session service logged last-active at 02:20:11. Looks like the session cache TTL didn't evict until the periodic sweep at 02:20. That could explain the 12m window. We should flag this as a least-privilege risk.

anya (security): Action items: 1) preserve KMS/HSM unwrap traces and export signed logs for 02:10-02:30 UTC (security holds) 2) prepare a short legal-facing timeline explaining cache TTL behavior and mitigation 3) confirm billing reconciliation steps to credit any duplicate token charges.

noah (eng-runtime): For mitigation: we can lower SCIM-to-session TTL from 15m to 30s for critical deprovs via a feature flag, but need a rollout plan. Also adding exponential backoff for client retries when 5xx is KMS-related should cut duplicate billing.

maria (support): Customer asked for repro steps we used. @tom @noah can you paste minimal repro they can run in staging (no keys involved) so they can validate fix?

tom (eng-sre): Repro (staging): 1) create tenant with embed traffic burst (~5K tokens/sec) 2) simulate KMS proxy latency (tc qdisc netem 200ms+ for HSM host) 3) send concurrent embed requests with client retry=2 -> observe 502s and repeated billed tokens in our test dashboard. I'll DM the exact script.

liam (cust-success): Thanks. Also, customer needs a billing contact to raise a refund claim. @finance or @billing?

maria (support): Looping in @anya for signed retention export + @billing for credits. audit-bot: request export job for tenant_acme_72 2024-10-11T02:10:00Z -> 2024-10-11T02:30:00Z, priority=high.

audit-bot: export job queued: job_id=export_20241011_001 tenant=tenant_acme_72 range=02:10-02:30 UTC priority=high ETA ~15m

anya (security): I'll prepare the statement and hold the logs. @legal please standby, tagging internal channel.

maria (support): Customer pinged to say they'd like interim confirmation that we're preserving data. I sent: "We've placed a security hold and queued an audit export for the requested window. We'll follow up with a signed timeline and remediation plan." :thumbsup:

liam (cust-success): I'll follow up with the customer post-export and collect any additional request ids. Thanks everyone, keep me posted when export completes.

tom (eng-sre): update: unwrap traces located and saved to secure blobstore. starting billing reconciliation to identify duplicated token invoices.

audit-bot: export job export_20241011_001 completed. download_url=https://internal.blob/export_20241011_001 (access audit-only)

maria (support): Received export. scanning now for missing audit lines and attaching to the ticket.

anya (security): Signed timeline ready, will circulate to legal + cust success for review before sending to customer.

liam (cust-success): Great — closing loop after credits confirmed. :white_check_mark:
